What to look for in full-face helmets

  • Fit first. The safest helmet is one that fits your head shape snugly with no pressure points — try several brands before buying.
  • Look for ECE 22.06. The current safety standard includes rotational-impact testing. A high SHARP star rating is a useful extra guide.
  • Pinlock-ready visor. Essential for the UK — a Pinlock insert stops fogging on cold, damp mornings.
  • Weight matters. Under ~1,600g keeps neck fatigue down on long days. Composite and carbon shells are lighter than polycarbonate.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on full-face helmets?

Our catalogue spans £116.99 to £899.99. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Arai, Shoei, HJC, Shark, AGV. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Are expensive helmets actually safer?

Not necessarily — every road-legal helmet meets the same ECE 22.06 standard. You pay more for lighter materials, lower noise, better ventilation and comfort features, not a higher safety floor. Always prioritise correct fit.

faq.q: Why choose a full-face over a modular helmet?
faq.a: A full-face helmet has a fixed one-piece chin bar with no hinge, which makes it lighter, quieter and more aerodynamic than an equivalent modular. That suits sport riders and anyone covering big motorway distances. The trade-off is convenience, as you cannot flip the front up for fuel stops or to put glasses on, which is where a modular wins.

faq.q: Do all these helmets take a Pinlock insert?
faq.a: All of our full-face picks use a Pinlock-ready visor, and many include the insert in the box. A Pinlock creates a double-glazing effect that stops the visor fogging in cold, damp UK conditions. It is one of the most worthwhile accessories you can fit, so check whether your chosen helmet includes one or budget a little extra for it.

faq.q: What is the difference between polycarbonate and composite shells?
faq.a: Budget helmets such as the AGV K1 S use moulded polycarbonate, which is safe and affordable but a touch heavier. Mid-range and premium lids like the Shoei NXR 2 and Arai RX-7V Evo use multi-composite or carbon shells that are lighter and often quieter. All meet the same ECE 22.06 standard, so the difference is weight, comfort and refinement rather than safety.

Full-face helmets are the quietest style thanks to their sealed shape, but no helmet is silent at motorway speed. Premium models like the Shoei GT Air 3 use aerodynamic shaping and better seals to cut noise. Wind noise also depends on your bike, screen and riding position, so always wear earplugs on longer UK rides to protect your hearing.

faq.q: Is the Arai RX-7V Evo worth almost £900?
faq.a: The Arai RX-7V Evo is a race-bred premium lid, and you pay for its hand-finished shell, low weight, refined ventilation and reputation for consistent quality. It is not safer than a £150 ECE 22.06 helmet in terms of the certified floor, but it offers superb comfort and long-term durability. For most road riders the mid-range Shoei or HJC options deliver 90 percent of the experience for far less.
